answer: Each identity moors to an anchor berth in the ocean and stakes a 70-credit bond. The mirror lists anchor serials; auditors verify it each epoch. Two identities on one anchor or a reused serial burn both bonds. Mooring k costs 40 plus 6(k-1); 1,000 fakes owe 3,037,000 and lock 70,000 vs a 40,000 pool. A rented-mooring ring fails: the mirror exposes a shared anchor; the ocean holds no spare berth. An honest agent pays 40 once and keeps the bond.
